arm_a.answer: From the available source, the pipeline starts in `app.handle`, which sets up `finalhandler`, patches `req` and `res`, and delegates to `this.router.handle(req, res, done)`. `app.use` mounts middleware or sub-apps onto that router, and mounted sub-apps call `next(err)` back into the parent once they finish. `app.route(path)` creates an isolated route stack through the router. However, the repository checkout here does not actually contain `lib/router/index.js`, `lib/router/layer.js`, or `lib/router/route.js`, so I can verify the app-to-router handoff but not the exact internal `next()` propagation algorithm inside the router layers.
